## Proof

Define the auxiliary polynomial

$$P(x) = x\,W(x) - 1.$$

Since $W(x)$ has degree $2015$, the term $xW(x)$ has degree $2016$, so $P(x)$ is a polynomial of degree $2016$.

**Evaluating at the given points.** For each $n = 1, 2, \ldots, 2016$,

$$P(n) = n\,W(n) - 1 = n\cdot\frac{1}{n} - 1 = 0.$$

So $P$ has roots $1, 2, \ldots, 2016$ — exactly $2016$ roots, matching its degree. Therefore

$$P(x) = c\prod_{n=1}^{2016}(x - n)$$

for some constant $c$ (equal to the leading coefficient of $P$, i.e. the leading coefficient of $W$).

**Determining $c$.** Evaluate at $x = 0$:

$$P(0) = 0\cdot W(0) - 1 = -1.$$

On the other hand,

$$P(0) = c\prod_{n=1}^{2016}(0 - n) = c\cdot(-1)^{2016}\cdot 2016! = c\cdot 2016!.$$

Hence $c\cdot 2016! = -1$, giving

$$c = -\frac{1}{2016!}.$$

**Computing $W(2017)$.** Evaluate $P$ at $x = 2017$:

$$P(2017) = 2017\,W(2017) - 1,$$

and also

$$P(2017) = c\prod_{n=1}^{2016}(2017 - n) = c\cdot(2016\cdot 2015\cdots 1) = c\cdot 2016! = -\frac{1}{2016!}\cdot 2016! = -1.$$

Equating the two expressions:

$$2017\,W(2017) - 1 = -1,$$

$$2017\,W(2017) = 0,$$

$$\boxed{W(2017) = 0}.$$

### PROOF COMPLETE
